title: Model rollforward - KV cache serialization timeout postmortem
summary: During a controlled rollforward of model v1.9.0 to canary nodes, a change to the KV cache serialization format caused repeated timeouts when canaries attempted to hydrate long-lived conversation caches. The canary healthchecks failed, traffic diversion triggered fallbacks to stable model variants, and the rollout was aborted and rolled back. No customer data loss was detected but latency and error spikes affected 0.6% of API requests for ~22 minutes.
impact: Approximately 0.6% of requests experienced increased 5xx errors and token-level latencies spiking by 2-3x for 22 minutes during the canary rollout window. Most affected were chat endpoints with long context (>8k tokens). No persisted customer KV data was corrupted; failures were transient timeouts.
detection: Automated canary health dashboard alerted at 2024-10-31T14:03:12Z when canary failure rate exceeded threshold. On-call SRE notebook recorded the alert; paging triggered. Observability showed elevated syscall timeouts in serialization stack and backend logs included repeated "kv_serialize: write timeout" errors.
timeline:
2024-10-31T13:50Z - Rollforward job started using serving-runtime:v2024.10.13 and model v1.9.0 on canary pool
2024-10-31T13:53Z - First canary instance failed liveness probe; autoscaler pulled additional canaries into the pool
2024-10-31T13:58Z - Health dashboards show error rate creeping up, SLO alert threshold crossed
2024-10-31T14:03Z - Pager triggered for on-call SRE rotation; incident channel created (#sre-incident-1324)
2024-10-31T14:06Z - On-call run initial triage: identify kv_serialize timeouts and elevated aio write latencies on canary hosts
2024-10-31T14:12Z - Decision point: stop traffic to canaries and abort rollout; rollback to model v1.8.7 confirmed at 14:15Z
2024-10-31T14:18Z - Canary pool health returns to baseline, client-facing metrics normalize by 14:25Z
2024-10-31T15:00Z - Post-incident sync scheduled and preliminary notes captured
root_cause: A codepath change in serving-runtime's KV cache serializer introduced an optional metadata header that increased the size and write-time of serialization operations for large conversation caches. On certain kernel/ioctl configurations (observed on canary image version with upgraded OS packages), large writes triggered a pathological fallback in the async writer that blocked the serialization thread for longer than the canary liveness timeout, producing timeouts and cascading request failures.
contributing_factors: 1) The serializer change was not covered by an existing long-context load test; CI only exercised small-conversation cases. 2) Canary pool used a newer OS image with subtly different aio behavior; infra change was not annotated as a risk for this rollout. 3) Healthcheck thresholds for canary liveness were aggressive for serialization stalls, causing early failure rather than graceful retry.
immediate_mitigation: Abort rollforward and rollback model version to v1.8.7 on canary and then resume canary gating off. Throttled canary traffic and temporarily increased canary liveness timeout to reduce flapping while rollback propagated. Alerted internal customers and support with expected ETA for full resolution.
rollback_notes: Rollback executed via rollout-control job at 2024-10-31T14:12Z; all canary instances replaced within 3 minutes. No manual intervention required for customer data stores. Verified sanity by re-running a sample set of long-context evals against v1.8.7; responses matched baseline latencies.
postmortem_findings:
- The serializer header change increased median serialization time for >8k token caches by ~85ms on affected hosts.
- The new OS aio behavior amplified tail latency, leading to blocked writes when multiple large serializations coincided.
- CI gap: no perf regression test for long-conversation cache serialization in PR acceptance pipeline.
- Risk annotation: infra patch that bumped kernel packages on canaries was deployed two days earlier without tagging as a rollout dependency.
remediation_and_actions:
1) Revert serializer header change in serving-runtime branch until a compatible async writer is implemented (PR referenced).
2) Add a long-context KV serialization perf test to CI that simulates >8k token caches and asserts P95 serialization <200ms.
3) Add an infra gate: any OS/kernel/upstream package changes must be tagged on rollout tickets for model changes.
4) Adjust default canary liveness threshold to tolerate short serialization stalls and rely on request-level retries instead of immediate liveness kills.
5) Create a diagnostic flag exposing serialization size histograms to dashboards for early detection.
runbook_updates:
- New checklist: before model rollforward, run 'kv-serialize-long-context' test on target canary OS image.
- Healthcheck tuning guidance: increase serialization-tolerant liveness timeout to 500ms for pools expected to handle >8k contexts.
- Add step to annotate infra package changes on rollout tickets and require signoff from infra owner.
- Include a quick command in runbook to migrate canaries to stable OS image if an infra mismatch is suspected.
follow_up_tickets: SRE-1329: Add KV long-context perf test to CI
SRV-490: Revert serializer header and implement non-blocking writer
OPS-214: Rollout infra gating for package upgrades
lessons_learned:
- Small API or metadata changes can have outsized impact when they change payload sizes for hot codepaths.
- Canary pools should mirror stable infra images closely; even minor libc/aio differences can manifest under tail load.
- Invest in targeted perf tests for long-tail contexts that align to customer workloads.
on_call_notes: Initial triage: check for 'kv_serialize: write timeout' in canary logs and correlate with host /proc/interrupts and aio metrics. If found, stop rollout and rollback via rollout-control. If rollback fails, escalate to infra for host-level remediation. For customer comms, use status.redwood/message with incident summary and ETA.
